statement: Unitary and Bilateral Boundedness Grade-Character Criteria (Theorems A and B) and Canonical Norm Audit: For a nontrivial zero rho = 1/2 + delta + i*gamma and canonical grade character chi_rho(K) = tau^(K*(rho-1/2)) = exp(K*(delta+i*gamma)*log tau) with modulus |chi_rho(K)| = tau^(K*delta) (tau = 2pi > 1), chi_rho takes values in the unit circle for all K in Integer (or at any single nonzero grade K != 0) if and only if delta = 0 (Theorem A). Furthermore, the character sequence is bounded over the full bilateral group Integer (sup_{K in Integer} |chi_rho(K)| < infinity) if and only if delta = 0 (Theorem B), where forward grades K >= 0 force delta <= 0 and backward grades K <= 0 force delta >= 0. In an audit across five canonical norm and space models (Intrinsic scalar norm, Multiplicative Haar dilation on L^2(R^+, dx/x), Group C*-algebra C*(Z), Explicit formula and Weil positivity, Alternative weighted norms and Davenport-Heilbronn countermodel), TC does not supply an independent proof that the zeta zero character must belong to the unitary or bounded class, leaving the prime-zero membership bridge as an open conditional premise.

quantified_variables.name: delta
quantified_variables.description: Real displacement from the critical line

hypotheses: chi_rho(K) = q_rho^K = tau^(K*(rho - 1/2)) = exp(K*(delta + i*gamma)*log tau)
object_studied: Canonical TC grade characters chi_rho(K) = q_rho^K and candidate normed Hilbert and Banach spaces
fourier_normalization: Centered coordinates z = s - 1/2 = delta + it; tau = 2pi
multiplicity_convention: Standard zero multiplicities m_rho in Integer_{>=1}
measure_and_window: Haar counting measure on Integer; Haar multiplicative measure dx/x on R^+
order_of_limits: Supremum over integer grades K in Integer; pointwise complex evaluation
exact_conclusion: Theorem A (|chi_rho(K)| = 1 iff delta = 0) and Theorem B (sup_{K in Integer} |chi_rho(K)| < infinity iff delta = 0) are exact proved criteria; the prime-zero membership bridge is conditional only as none of the five canonical models independently forces character boundedness without assuming RH
logical_negation: There exists delta != 0 with |chi_rho(K)| = 1 for K != 0, or sup_{K in Integer} |chi_rho(K)| < infinity with delta != 0, or TC independently forces character boundedness on zeta zeros without assuming RH (FALSIFIED / REFUTED)
falsification_attempts: Symbolic elimination and equality-case cancellation analysis: solved |tau^(K*delta)| = 1 in SymPy, proving the unique cancellation root is delta = 0 for any non-zero grade K != 0 and tau > 1

Asymptotic dominance and boundary limit audit: evaluated bilateral divergence in the asymptotic limits K -> +infinity for delta > 0 and K -> -infinity for delta < 0, proving bilateral Integer is strictly necessary to force delta = 0

Audited Davenport-Heilbronn zeta function: verified that off-line zeros satisfy functional equation and dilation symmetry but have non-unitary, unbounded grade characters, excluding functional equation symmetry as an independent source of unitarity
Audited Weil positivity equivalence: confirmed that assuming explicit formula character positivity is circularly equivalent to assuming RH (Weil 1952)
Audited C*(Z) group algebra: confirmed that restricting chi_rho to C*(Z) characters circularly assumes delta = 0 a priori
